When the verses of Al-Baqara on usury were revealed, the Prophet recited them to the people in the mosque and then banned the trade in alcohol.
People will not care if gain is lawful; the Prophet banned alcohol trade, dreamt of a riba-eater stoned in a river of blood, and forbade dog prices, tattooing and riba.
Wheat for wheat, barley for barley and dates for dates are riba unless equal in amount and handed over hand to hand.
Gold for gold, silver for silver, must be equal and hand to hand, else riba; gold for silver is allowed, not on credit; Ibn Abbas saw riba only in delay.
Learning Khaibar's governor bartered one sa of fine dates for two, the Prophet forbade it as a kind of usury: sell the mixed dates for money, then buy good ones.
The Prophet forbids exchanging two Sa of poor dates for one of good Janib dates as Riba: sell the poor dates for money and buy with it.
Bilal exchanges two Sa of poor dates for one of Barni dates, and the Prophet says it is Riba: sell the poor dates for money, then buy.
When the verses of Al-Baqara on usury were revealed the Prophet recited them and prohibited trade in alcohol; Ibn Abbas said the usury verse was the last revealed.
